policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'into the synagogue' supplies the English definite article either way; the presence or absence of Greek τὴν is invisible in the rendering.
Aorist subjunctive κατηγορήσωσιν and future κατηγορήσουσιν after ἵνα are both rendered 'that they might accuse him'; the English does not distinguish.

'the man that had his hand withered' renders any of the three: the adjective ξηράν and the perfect participle ἐξηραμμένην alike give 'withered', and the Greek word order leaves no trace in the English.
Ἔγειρε and Ἔγειραι are the same imperative in different form; ASV 'Stand forth' (note: Greek Arise into the midst) does not distinguish them.
ἀγαθοποιῆσαι and ἀγαθὸν ποιῆσαι are both 'to do good'; the compound versus the periphrasis is not visible in the English.
ASV 'Stretch forth thy hand' is its ordinary rendering of the Greek article with a body part, so 'thy' does not establish that σου stood in the text; no note bears on the unit.
ASV ends the verse at 'and his hand was restored', with no equivalent of ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη ('whole as the other'), so the shorter reading is the one rendered.
εὐθὺς and εὐθέως are both rendered 'straightway'; the English does not distinguish the two forms.
συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν and συμβούλιον ἐποίουν are both idioms for 'took counsel', which is what ASV prints; neither is excluded.
All three readings contain the same words; ASV 'Jesus with his disciples withdrew to the sea' follows English order and does not report the Greek placement of ἀνεχώρησεν.
ASV reads 'a great multitude from Galilee followed' with no object; it renders nothing for the αὐτῷ of ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ, so the shorter reading is the one behind the English.
The added article οἱ before a place phrase has no English exponent in 'and from Jerusalem'; the only note here is an alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.
As with the parallel unit, the article οἱ is not rendered separately in ASV's series of place phrases; nothing in the English distinguishes the readings.
ASV 'hearing what great things he did' translates either the present ἀκούοντες or the aorist ἀκούσαντες; an English present participle is ASV's usual rendering for both.
ASV 'what great things he did' is past; the present ποιεῖ would give 'he doeth', so the imperfect ἐποίει is the reading rendered.

The subject τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα is neuter plural, which regularly takes singular verbs in Greek and is rendered plural in English regardless; ASV 'whensoever they beheld him, fell down' therefore does not exclude the singular verbs, and the readings otherwise differ only in punctuation.
Same neuter plural subject: ἔκραζεν and ἔκραζον are both rendered 'and cried' after 'the unclean spirits', so number is not recoverable from the English.
λέγοντα and λέγοντες differ only in the gender of the participle; both are 'saying' in ASV.
Word order only: 'that they should not make him known' fixes English order and reports nothing about the Greek sequence of αὐτὸν and φανερὸν.
ποιήσωσιν and ποιῶσιν are aorist and present subjunctive of the same verb; ASV 'should not make' does not distinguish aspect here.

ASV text reads 'And he appointed twelve, that they might be with him' with no 'whom also he named apostles', and its textual_variant note assigns that clause to 'some ancient authorities' — the margin, not the text.
ASV 'and to have authority to cast out demons' has no equivalent of θεραπεύειν τὰς νόσους καὶ ('to heal diseases and'), so the shorter reading is rendered.
ASV text runs straight to 'and Simon he surnamed Peter' and its textual_variant note says 'Some ancient authorities insert and he appointed twelve' — the clause is absent from the text ASV rendered.
Word order only within ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι; ASV 'and Simon he surnamed Peter' recasts the clause entirely.

ASV 'them he surnamed Boanerges' renders the idiom without a countable noun, so ὀνόματα (plural) and ὄνομα (singular) are equally compatible; the two notes are alternative_rendering and cannot decide.
ASV prints 'Simon the Cananaean', the transliteration of Καναναῖον; Κανανίτην would give 'Canaanite'. The note 'Or, Zealot' glosses the same form.
Ἰσκαριώθ and the declined Ἰσκαριώτην are both transliterated 'Iscariot'; the two notes are alternative_rendering and bear on 'betrayed' and 'a house', not on this unit.

The ASV of 3:20 shown here begins 'And the multitude cometh together again', which renders συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος; nothing in this verse renders the verb of this unit, so its number is undetermined from the English before me.
ASV 'the multitude' uses the English article whether or not Greek ὁ stood; the article's presence is not recoverable.
μηδὲ and μήτε are both rendered by 'not so much as' in 'they could not so much as eat bread'.
ASV 'that house will not be able to stand' is future, matching δυνήσεται; the present δύναται would give 'cannot stand', which is exactly how ASV renders the present in v. 26.
στῆναι and σταθῆναι are both 'to stand', and the placement of ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη is not reported by the English order 'that house will not be able to stand'.
ASV 'and is divided' fits the aorist ἐμερίσθη and the perfect μεμέρισται alike; no tense distinction survives in the English.
στῆναι and σταθῆναι are alternative aorist infinitives both rendered 'stand' in 'he cannot stand'.
ASV begins 'But no one can enter', rendering ἀλλ᾽, which the RP reading lacks; between the two readings that keep ἀλλ᾽ only the order of οὐδεὶς and δύναται differs, and that is invisible in English.
Word order only: 'enter into the house of the strong man, and spoil his goods' is the natural English sequence under either arrangement of the same words.
ASV 'and then he will spoil his house' renders the future διαρπάσει and the aorist subjunctive διαρπάσῃ alike; a subjunctive in this apodosis is regularly Englished as a future.
Both readings hold the same words; ASV 'shall be forgiven unto the sons of men' places the phrases by English syntax and does not report the Greek order.
The article αἱ and the ὅσα ἐὰν / ὅσας ἂν variation are both absorbed by 'and their blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme'.
ASV 'is guilty of an eternal sin' renders αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος; κρίσεως would give 'eternal judgment' or 'condemnation', which ASV does not print.
ASV 'And there come his mother and his brethren' has the connective 'And' (καὶ, not οὖν) and a plural verb 'come'; that excludes both Ἔρχονται οὖν and the singular ἔρχεται, leaving Καὶ ἔρχονται.
ASV names them in the order 'his mother and his brethren', matching ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ; the RP reading reverses the two, and coordinate proper subjects are rendered in Greek order.
στήκοντες and ἑστῶτες are both rendered 'standing without'.
καλοῦντες and φωνοῦντες are both rendered 'calling him'.
Word order only: 'a multitude was sitting about him' follows English syntax whichever Greek arrangement stood.
ASV 'and they say unto him' has the connective 'and' and a present tense, matching καὶ λέγουσιν; εἶπον δὲ would give 'but they said'.
ASV reads 'thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee' with no 'and thy sisters', so the addition καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαί σου is not in the text rendered.
ASV 'And he answereth them, and saith' has both verbs in the present, matching ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει; ἀπεκρίθη ... λέγων would give 'he answered them, saying'.
ASV 'Who is my mother and my brethren?' joins the two with 'and' (καὶ); ἢ would give 'or'.
ASV renders a possessive with each noun, 'my mother and my brethren'; the omission would leave one of the pair without 'my'.
Word order only: 'them that sat round about him' renders the same words in either Greek arrangement.
ASV begins the verse 'For whosoever shall do the will of God', rendering γὰρ; the omission would leave no connective.
ASV's single possessive in 'my brother, and sister, and mother' governs the whole series, so it neither requires nor excludes a second μου after ἀδελφή.
